from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load Assets
        bulb = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bulb.svg")

        screen = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/screen.svg")
        laser = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg")
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(bulb, "A2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(bulb), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Represent wave propagation patterns with barrier
        self.place_at_grid(barrier, "B2", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(barrier), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Interference fringes on screen
        self.place_at_grid(screen, "C5", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(screen), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Coherent frequency color change for bulb
        self.play(bulb.animate.set_color(GREEN), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(GREEN))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Laser morph
        self.place_at_grid(laser, "E5", scale_factor=0.3)
        self.play(FadeIn(laser), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Photographs capture only light intensity.",
            "Holography records the interference pattern.",
            "Reference beams provide constant phase.",
            "Object beams reflect off the subject.",
            "Interference freezes phase data on film."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Holography Mechanism: Recording", lecture_lines)
        
        # Assets
        laser = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/laser.svg")
        film = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/film.svg")
        subject = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/subject.svg")
        
        # Elements
        ref_beam = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=YELLOW)
        obj_beam = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*1.5, color=RED)
        fringe = Rectangle(width=1.5, height=2.5, color=PURPLE).set_fill(PURPLE, opacity=0.4)
        
        # Position Assets and Elements
        self.place_at_grid(laser, 'D2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(film, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(subject, 'C3', 'C4', scale_factor=0.4)
        
        self.place_at_grid(ref_beam, 'B3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(obj_beam, 'E3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(laser), FadeIn(film), FadeIn(subject))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(GrowArrow(ref_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        self.play(GrowArrow(obj_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(film.copy(), fringe))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Holography and Diffraction

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
sections.content: Briefly review wave superposition and phase coherence. Explain that light is an electromagnetic wave characterized by amplitude and phase (the 'position' of the wave peak).
sections.example: Visualizing a ripple in a pond: how two ripples meeting create a complex pattern of peaks and troughs (constructive vs. destructive interference).

sections.title: Understanding Diffraction
sections.content: Define diffraction as the bending of waves around obstacles. Introduce the mathematical concept using the Fourier Transform: the diffraction pattern is the spatial frequency representation of the object.
sections.example: A laser pointer shining through a thin mesh (like a screen door) to produce a grid of dots—the 'diffraction pattern' encodes the shape of the mesh.

sections.title: The Holography Mechanism: Recording
sections.content: Explain that while photos only capture intensity (amplitude), holography captures interference patterns. Introduce the 'Reference Beam' vs. 'Object Beam' concept to record phase information.
sections.example: An animation showing two light waves meeting on a photographic plate, creating a 'frozen' interference pattern that looks like static noise but contains 3D data.

sections.title: The Holography Mechanism: Reconstruction
sections.content: Explain that shining the original reference beam back through the developed hologram acts like a 'key,' diffracting the light to recreate the original wavefronts.
sections.example: Imagine a 3D hologram of a rotating Iron Man helmet: as you walk around the hologram, you see different sides of the helmet because the phase-encoded light reconstructs the original spatial volume.

sections.title: Synthesis and Applications
sections.content: Connect the math (Fourier optics) to real-world technology. Summarize how diffraction enables the storage of 3D space on a 2D surface.
sections.example: Modern applications: Holographic data storage for long-term archival or high-security authentication on credit cards.
